claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons possess inherent local phase inhomogeneity.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi contains locally mixed cation valence states, especially involving Mn.
Nanoscale phase and valence inhomogeneity creates regions with distinct magnetic exchange interactions.
The spatially distinct exchange interactions govern the magnetocaloric response of nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi.
The spatially distinct exchange interactions govern magnetic hysteresis in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi.
A rapid low-temperature anneal will cause limited cation diffusion in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi.
A rapid low-temperature anneal will homogenize the local cation and phase distribution.
The proposed anneal can achieve homogenization without significant grain growth.
Mixed-valence states produce spatially variable exchange bias.
Mixed-valence states produce magnetic frustration.
Spatially variable exchange bias and magnetic frustration broaden magnetic hysteresis.
Spatially variable exchange bias and magnetic frustration diminish the magnetocaloric effect.
Annealing-induced cation uniformity reduces local magnetic discontinuities.
Annealing-induced cation uniformity enhances heat-transfer kinetics during a magnetic-cooling cycle.
Annealed samples will have narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than otherwise identical as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric response and better cooling performance than as-deposited samples.
Annealing will improve the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Heat-transfer rates are rate limiting for the proposed near-ambient magnetic-cooling cycles.
An analogous Mn-containing high-entropy oxide thin film contains coexisting rock-salt and spinel-like regions.
The analogous Mn-containing high-entropy oxide thin film exhibits mixed Co and Mn valence states together with greater exchange bias and magnetic frustration than the Cr-containing comparator.
